evidence_spans.quote: Deep Learning, Predictability, and Optimal Portfolio Returns
We study the dynamic portfolio selection of an investor who uses deep learning methods to fore- cast stock market excess returns.
uses deep learning methods to fore- cast stock market excess returns
There are two assets: a one-period Treasury bill and a stock index.
Panel A: 6-month horizon and quarterly rebalancing

uses deep learning methods to fore- cast stock market excess returns
The forecast starts in February 1955. The sample period spans from January 1945 to December 2018.
exploiting the time-series structure of standard predictor variables via deep learning
including a long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent architecture

At the end of each quarter (year), we split the data into training and validation samples that maintain the temporal ordering of the data and tune hyperparameters with respect to the statistical and economic criteria.

To fit the networks, we adopt a popular and robust adaptive moment estimation algorithm (Adam) with weight decay regularization introduced by Kingma and Ba (2014) and we use the Huber loss function in the estimation.
Since the sample at each window is rather small and final models can depend on initial values in the optimization, we use ensemble averaging of five models with randomly chosen initial values.
Panels A and B show the MSPE and out-of-sampleR 2 statistics based on those periods when quarterly and annual rebalancing happens.
